records.quote: Counterexample 3.1. Consider the baseline distribution function as Fb(x) = 1 - exp(1 - x^a), x >= 1, a > 0. For this, when 0 < a <= 1, the hazard rate function is decreasing. Let {X1, X2, X3} and {Y1, Y2, Y3} be the collections of dependent random variables with Xi ~ Fb^alpha((x - lambda_i)/theta) and Yi ~ Fb^alpha((x - mu_i)/theta), for i = 1, 2, 3 with generators psi_1(x) = e^{(1/a1)(1 - e^x)} and psi_2(x) = e^{(1/a2)(1 - e^x)}, respectively, where x > 0, 0 < a1, a2 <= 1. Here, psi_1 and psi_2 both are log-concave. Assume a1 = 0.001 and a2 = 0.5. Then, phi_2 o psi_1(x) is sub-additive, and hence is not super-additive. Set lambda = (3, 4, 5), mu = (6, 7, 8), theta = 6, alpha = 8 and a = 0.9. Thus, all the conditions of Theorem 3.17 are satisfied except super-additivity of phi_2 o psi_1(x) and the restriction on alpha. Now, we plote the graphs of Fbar_{X_{2:3}}(x) and Fbar_{Y_{2:3}}(x) in Figure 2a. The graphs cross each other, which implies that Theorem 3.17 does not hold.
records.family: dependent ELS marginals Xi ~ Fb^alpha((x - lambda_i)/theta) with Archimedean generators psi_1(x) = e^{(1/a1)(1 - e^x)}, psi_2(x) = e^{(1/a2)(1 - e^x)}; baseline Fb(x) = 1 - exp(1 - x^a), x >= 1 (lower-truncated Weibull)
records.compared: location vectors lambda = (3,4,5) vs mu = (6,7,8); common scale theta = 6; generators a1 = 0.001 vs a2 = 0.5; alpha = 8 vs required <= 1

hypotheses.text: all the conditions of Theorem 3.17 are satisfied except super-additivity of phi_2 o psi_1(x) and the restriction on alpha
hypotheses.formal: violates phi_2 o psi_1 super-additivity (it is sub-additive) and alpha <= 1 (alpha = 8)

hypotheses.text: mu <<w lambda => X_{2:n} <=st Y_{2:n}, provided psi_1 or psi_2 is log-concave (Theorem 3.17)
hypotheses.formal: the theorem's hypotheses: alpha = beta = alpha 1_n <= 1, theta = delta, phi_2 o psi_1 super-additive, lambda, mu in I+ (or D+), r_b decreasing, log-concave generator

conclusion.direction: negated: Fbar_{X_{2:3}}(x) and Fbar_{Y_{2:3}}(x) cross (Figure 2a), so neither X_{2:3} <=st Y_{2:3} nor the reverse holds

records.numbers: a1 = 0.001; a2 = 0.5; lambda = (3,4,5); mu = (6,7,8); theta = 6; alpha = 8; a = 0.9; Fb(x) = 1 - exp(1 - x^a), x >= 1; Figure 2a shows crossing survival curves
records.ambiguity: Refutes Theorem 3.17 when super-additivity and alpha <= 1 are dropped. Typo 'plote' is verbatim. With lambda = (3,4,5) and mu = (6,7,8), the weak-majorization hypothesis mu <<w lambda also appears to fail under the usual convention (mu has the larger partial sums), so the example may violate more than the two conditions the authors list.

note: Paper prints crossing survival curves of X_{2:3} and Y_{2:3} (Figure 2a): the st conclusion of Theorem 3.17 fails; both passes' dir labels were normalization artifacts of the same 'no order' substance.
